observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South: a slim, long-legged hoofed grazer seen head-on, with a tall pale-grey mineral club rising from the skull and a long narrow face toward the camera. The neck, chest and shoulders are studded with raised domed boils in mauve, brown and ochre. East: a full side profile of a deer-like body walking right. The coat is grey-brown, darker on the back and paler on the belly. Rounded boils of many sizes cover the back, flanks, neck and haunches; the boils are glossy purple-brown with ochre rims. The legs are slender with dark hooves, and the tail is short and tufted. A single knobbed, crusted grey club with spiky points sweeps back from the head. North: the rear, showing the haunches, a short tail flap and the back of the neck covered in boils. The club shows as a V-shaped pair of lobes above the head. No face or eyes. All three facings are the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. The face looks at the camera and the eyes are small and dull. The club is a stacked, layered crust of grey mineral above the brow. Boils cover the neck and chest and are larger on the shoulders. The legs are thin and grey-brown. Clean alpha, with nothing under the hooves.
observed.east.png: Side profile looking right. The animal stands with a walking gait. Dense domed boils cover the dorsal half and the neck; the belly and legs are smooth grey. The club is fused from the skull into one mass, crusted pale grey with darker spurs along its rear edge. It reads as one mineral club, not a branching rack. The painterly shading is realistic. A thin dark edge follows the silhouette, the same as on the kept adult. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Rows of boils run along the spine and haunches, and a short tail hangs between the hind legs. The back of the club shows as a split two-lobed crest above the neck. No face and no eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal stands about as tall as the vanilla human, within one cell. At normal play (32 px/cell) the inset shows a small brown-grey quadruped with a pale club, darker than the dirt. The body reads, but the thin legs and the boils fade.
observed.siblings.png: The kept adult: the same anatomy, pose, club and silhouette, but with a pale grey-white hide and saturated purple boils with bright yellow highlights. The candidate matches this layout pose for pose; only the palette differs.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the haunches, tail and back of the club lobes. There is no face and there are no eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn at the standing game angle. None is a top-down view.

SIGNATURE.seen: The sealed boils covering the hide are the dominant read on every facing, and the fused crusted club is plain on the head.

ALIEN.seen: The body is deer-like, but the dense domed boils and the single mineral club replace the identity a stranger would give a deer. The design matches the owner-kept adult, which shares this body plan.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Boils cover the hide: present on the back, flanks, neck, chest and haunches; the belly and lower legs are smooth, as on the kept adult. 2) The antlers are fused into one mineral-crusted club: present, a single crusted grey mass with no separate tines.

STYLE.seen: Painterly realistic shading with dull eyes. Not cute, not cel-shaded, not a photo or render. The thin edge is the same as on the kept sibling.

OURS.seen: The art is bespoke and matches the RimMandrake adult. No vanilla or other-mod donor art.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is clean on all three facings, with no ground, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the adult in siblings.png, in a distinct colouring: a grey-brown hide with mauve-brown, ochre-rimmed boils against the adult's pale hide with purple and yellow boils.

SCALE.seen: About human height at drawSize 0.9. The description gives no size words, and the size matches the adult sibling.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px the darker body and pale club separate from the dirt. The read is weaker than the pale adult's, but it is still a quadruped silhouette.

findings.seen: The grey-brown hide and brown boils sit closer in value to the brown soil than the pale adult does. At 32 px the boils merge into the body, and the thin legs nearly vanish.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a squat, wide armoured quadruped seen head-on with the head lowered; overlapping dark brown and grey plates with tan edges fan out over the back and shoulders; the underbody and legs are pale grey; there are four hooved feet. East: a long, low, heavy-bodied grazer in side profile with its head down near the ground; large overlapping brown plates with ochre-tan streaks run in shingled tiers from the tail to the head; small pale lichen-like rosettes and round pock holes mark the plates; the hide is wrinkled pinkish-brown with dark mottling; the legs are thick and hooved. North: the rear of the animal, with stacked plates narrowing to a segmented, plated tail stub between the thick hind legs; the plates are pale grey-white with lichen mottling and pock holes; the hind legs are tan with dark blotches; there is no face. The sprites have no outlines, and the alpha is clean.
observed.south.png: A front view at full resolution. The head is lowered toward the camera, with a plated brow and snout, two small dark eyes, and a split lip or tusk-like plates at the chin. Tiered plates rise over the shoulders in a pointed mound. The plates are dark grey-brown with tan rims and a few round pock holes. The legs and belly are pale grey with wrinkled skin. There is no ground shadow.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right, head down to graze. About seven tiers of large overlapping plates are shingled along the back, each brown with ochre streaks; several round dark pock marks with raised rims sit on the plates; small cream lichen rosettes are scattered over them. Smaller plates cover the neck and head. The skin is wrinkled pinkish-brown with darker blotches. The hooves are dark. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: A rear view. Plates stack in tiers up to a peak, with a small plated tail of segments hanging between the hind legs. The plates here are distinctly pale grey-white with dark lichen-like mottling and pock holes, a lighter and greyer palette than the brown plates on east and south. The hind legs are tan with dark spots. There are no eyes or face.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the chatrak is about 3 cells long and about 1.5 cells tall beside a vanilla human, so it is bigger than the human: a large, low grazer. At 32 px per cell it reads as a long, low, plated grey-brown hump with legs, distinct from the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult chatrak: the same anatomy, pose and silhouette on every facing (head-down grazer, shingled tiered plates, plated tail stub). Its colouring is blue-grey steel plates with rust-orange edges and pocks, over pale tan skin. It has a heavy black outline around the whole silhouette.

SIGNATURE.seen: Low plated grazer with its head down; tiered back plates that read like an earthwork are clear on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The body reads as a heavy rhino-like grazer under shingled pangolin-like plate tiers, with ricochet pocks. It matches the owner-kept adult's anatomy, and a stranger would not name a single Earth species at first glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: Tiered plates like an earthwork: present (about seven shingled tiers on east, stacked tiers on south and north). Plates pocked by ricochets: present (round rimmed pock holes on the plates of all three facings).

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic: wrinkled skin, weathered plate texture. Not cute, not cel-shaded, no keyline, not a photo or a 3D render.

OURS.seen: A new colouring of the mod's own chatrak anatomy; no vanilla or other-mod animal.

SCALE.seen: About 3 cells long and taller than the human's torso at max zoom, which fits a large, low grazer with drawSize 3.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a long, low, plated hump on legs, apart from the ground.

invariants: Body plan from the east facing: a low, broad plated grazer, head carried down
Back plates stacked in tiers like an earthwork, pocked by bullet ricochets

Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges, value and colour contrast carrying the silhouette

request.prompt:
A single chatrak, a low plated grazer, painted as one animal in one fixed colour scheme. Top-down three-quarter game sprite for RimWorld, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Transparent background.

Body: low, broad and heavy, four short thick legs, head carried down as it grazes at rust-orange lichen. The back is covered by plates stacked in tiers like an earthwork, each tier overlapping the one behind it. The plates are pocked with small pale ricochet scars and dents from bullets. The hide turns bullets and the animal looks calm and unbothered.

Palette, identical on every facing: the back plates are warm brown with ochre streaks and cream lichen rosettes. The exposed skin and legs are pinkish-brown and mottled. The rust-orange lichen near the mouth is the only strongly orange note. Lighting changes only the value of these colours, lighter on the lit side and darker on the shaded side. The hue and material of the plates, streaks, rosettes, skin and legs stay the same in every view.

Facings: the east view is a side view with the head to the right, showing the tiered plates in profile. The south view is a front view, eyes toward the viewer, head low, plates rising behind it, with the same warm brown plates and pinkish-brown mottled legs. The north view is a rear view, seen from behind: the back, the plate tiers, the haunches and the short tail, eyes hidden, with the same warm brown plates with ochre streaks and cream rosettes over the same pinkish-brown mottled hide. The ricochet pocks and lichen rosettes sit on the same plates in every facing.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of one quadruped on a checkerboard at one scale. The animal has long legs, a deep chest, a thick upright neck, a large head with a heavy grey hooked beak, a few small nubs on the crown and a short tail. The hide is fuzzy and fur-like, with large irregular ochre and rust patches like a giraffe's. The back rises gently from the rump to the withers and is rounded. There is no flat slab and no overhang. The east facing looks somewhat smaller overall than the south and north facings.
observed.south.png: Front view with the face toward the camera: two amber eyes under heavy brows, a central downturned hooked beak and small crown nubs. Broad chest, four legs with two-toed hoof-like feet. The expression is stern. Clean alpha. The hide is soft fur with patches.
observed.east.png: True right-facing side profile. The body is horse-, llama- or camel-like: a rounded back that rises slightly at the withers into a thick neck. observed.north.png: Rear view: rump, a short tapered tail, haunches and hind legs, and the back of the neck and head. No face and no eyes. Two curved hook-like projections stick out at each side of the head. These do not appear on the south or east views. The back reads as a rounded mound.

observed.siblings.png: Reference RM_Sollak, south, east and north. concerns.evidence: The juvenile has a rounded torso and softly textured patches, while the adult has a broad, projecting back slab and coarse stone-like hide. Those species-defining features are lost. The juvenile's shorter legs and larger head are appropriate to the owner note and are not themselves faults.

East shows a narrow, rounded back contour leading into the shoulder hump. North shows a rounded rump and tapering spinal ridge. Neither shows the adult reference's broad, flat slab with projecting edges.

Across the individual facings, the ochre and rust regions have soft, finely fuzzy surfaces and irregular coat-like boundaries. Visible fracture lines or hard stone plates are absent, especially across the east flank and north haunches.

East first reads as a camel-like juvenile quadruped: rounded barrel, raised withers, thick ascending neck and short tail. The hooked bird beak is conspicuous, but appears added to that familiar mammalian body rather than supported by the adult's unusual slab-backed anatomy.

The defining slab-flat back is absent in east and north. The concern overstates the other omissions: the raised shoulder hump and ochre/rust colouring are also present, alongside the beak and thick neck.

The candidate's softly blended, relatively uniform surface differs visibly from the adult reference's coarse, deeply shaded, angular surface. This supports a material and finish mismatch. The candidate's lack of an outline is correct under the style law and is not a fault.

On the shared-scale sheet, east has shorter, slimmer supporting limbs and a less substantial shoulder mass than the front and rear views. The forward neck angle explains some height reduction, but does not explain all the apparent reduction in body and limb scale. This supports the measured 29% spread.

North shows two substantial downward-curving projections flanking the skull. South has a clean lateral head silhouette without corresponding projections, and east lacks a matching projection behind the cheek or skull.

Gritty, high-texture painterly finish with coarse brushwork, deep crevice shading and a dark, muted earthy palette, matching the adult. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette against the ground.

All three views (front, side, rear) show the animal at the same scale: the same body height, shoulder mass, leg length, head size and hoof size. In the side view the neck extends forward while the shoulders and legs keep the full bulk seen in the front and rear views.

The head carries the same two small crown nubs in every view, rooted at the top of the skull, equal in size, pointing upward and slightly back. The rear view shows the back of the skull with those two nubs and nothing else at the sides of the head.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South and north are both about the same height and fill the panel. The creature is a stout, wrinkled, brown-grey, hairless-looking quadruped with a barrel body. It has thick pillar legs with toe pads, a broad hippo-like muzzle with heavy jowls, two small conical horns on the brow and a short tapering tail. The back has darker mottled patches. There is no carapace or mantle of any kind.
observed.south.png: A front view with the face toward the camera. The head is broad and low, with small brown eyes, two small blunt horns above the eyes, puffy cheek pouches and a drooping wrinkled upper lip like a hippo's muzzle. observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. The body is a long, low barrel with mottled dark brown dorsal patches over lighter tan flanks. A short tail points down and back. observed.facings.png: A squat, armoured, four-legged creature shown south, east and north at one scale on a checkerboard. Overlapping domed plates cover the back. The plates are olive-khaki with a strong oily rainbow sheen and crusted with pale, flaky mud. The legs are short and stout, with grey-brown wrinkled, tortoise-like skin and blunt toes. On east, the front narrows to a long, flat, pointed wedge plate over the snout, with a small dark eye under the plate edge. On south, a triangular plate points down over the face, with two small eyes under it. On north, the plates step down over the rump and the hind legs show from behind. North looks somewhat taller and wider than south, and east is lower and longer.
observed.south.png: Front view. A broad dome of overlapping plates, mud-crusted along the midline. A downward-pointing triangular blade plate sits over the face, with two small eyes visible beneath it. The front legs are splayed and stubby, with toes. Clean alpha, no ground.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. The body is a low wedge: high plated back at the rear, tapering forward into a long, flat, pointed blade head that sticks out past the front legs. An eye sits at the base of the blade. Three or four big overlapping plates run along the back, iridescent with mud crust. Four short wrinkled legs with blunt toes. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Stepped plates over the back with mud crust, the wrinkled rump skin below, two stout hind legs and the soles of the feet. No face, no eyes, no tail visible. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the candidate (east) is about two-thirds of a cell long and lower than the human's knee height, beside the human. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a small khaki wedge, a little smaller than the rat strip beside it, and reads as a light-brown lump with a pointed end.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult karrobel, south/east/north. Matte brown, banded segmented carapace like an isopod or arthropod. Many curved, claw-like legs along each side, no visible toes or tetrapod limbs. A large dark blade head plate. A thin dark outline. No iridescence. A wider, flatter, crab-like spread of legs.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front: the blade plate points down over the face, two eyes are visible beneath it, and the front legs face the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows stepped rear plates, the rump and the hind leg soles. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are at the low game-camera angle. None is top-down.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 36%. In facings.png, north is visibly bulkier than south and taller than east (east is about 126 px against north's 171 px). Part of this is pose, because the profile is long and low, but north against south and east still reads as a size step.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same plated, mud-crusted, iridescent animal with stubby toed legs appears on all three facings. The blade head shows as a down-pointing triangle on south and a forward wedge on east, and is hidden on north, so the blade head turns with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The hardened blade head is clear on east (a long pointed wedge) and visible on south. Mud-caked back plates are visible on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The body (dome shell, stumpy wrinkled toed legs) is tortoise-like. The forward blade head and the stacked iridescent plates break the tortoise read on east. On south and north, a stranger could say 'a turtle'. This is borderline, not a clear fail.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 thick wedge body: present on east (high rear tapering forward). 2 head as a hardened blade: present (long pointed plate on east, triangle on south). 3 banded, mud-caked back plates: mud-caked plates are present, but there are three or more plates rather than a pair, and the banding is weak (iridescent sheen rather than bands).

Side view: the long wedge in profile, with the blade head at the front, the row of claw legs along the visible flank, and the two banded plates in a row along the back. Rear view, seen from behind: the broad blunt end of the wedge with the two banded mud-caked plates on top and the claw-leg rows on both flanks. Single creature, centered, full body visible, 0.9 tile footprint.

edits.change: One fixed band sequence, head to tail, on every facing: warm rust-orange band on the shoulders just behind the head, then golden yellow, then deep teal, then violet purple, then a pale cream band at the tail tip. Each plate keeps its own colour whichever way the body turns.

Front view, seen from the head end: the head and shoulders face the viewer, and the rust-orange shoulder band is the only band fully visible, with the yellow band starting behind it. The violet and cream plates are hidden behind the body.

Side view, head to the right: the full sequence runs along the back from right to left in this order: rust-orange, golden yellow, deep teal, violet purple, cream tail tip. Five plates, each about equal in width.

Rear view, seen from behind: the cream tail tip is nearest the viewer, with the violet plate directly in front of it, then teal, then yellow. The rust-orange band shows only as a thin strip at the far shoulders, and the eyes are hidden.

Soft painted edges: each armour plate is separated from its neighbour by a darker value in the seam between the plates and a deep shadow value where the body meets the ground. Value and colour contrast carry the silhouette.

Match the adult's silhouette weight: the body edge reads dark and strong against a light ground because the outermost plates and the underside are painted in the darkest value of the body. The adult's heavy black contour is not copied.

A row of five pigment-banded plates runs down its back in one fixed order from head to tail: rust-orange on the shoulders just behind the head, then golden yellow, then deep teal, then violet purple, then pale cream at the tail tip. The five plates are about equal in width and each keeps its own colour on every view. Front view, seen from the head end: head and eyes toward the viewer, only the rust-orange shoulder band fully visible, the yellow band starting behind it. Side view, head to the right: the whole sequence reads along the back from right to left, rust-orange, golden yellow, deep teal, violet purple, cream tail tip. Rear view, seen from behind: the cream tail tip nearest the viewer, the violet plate directly in front of it, then teal, then yellow, with rust-orange only a thin strip at the far shoulders and the eyes hidden. Soft painted edges: darker values in the seams between plates and in the deep shadow of the underside and legs, so each plate is clearly separated from its neighbour. The outermost plates are painted in the darkest value of the body, so value and colour contrast carry the silhouette against the ground, matching the strong silhouette weight of the adult in siblings.png. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic. The anatomy, plate shape and base palette follow the previous render and the adult; the band colours and their order follow this prompt.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South: a rounded, barrel-bodied four-legged animal facing the camera. Its face has two small dark eyes and a cluster of thick, fleshy, finger-like tentacles hanging over the mouth. It has a small purple tuft or crest on its crown and thick, toed, elephant-like feet. East: a long, low, sausage-shaped quadruped walking right, with the same tentacled snout, short legs, a frilled, fan-like tail, and a small crest on the head. North: a tall, rounded rump with a broad purple ridge running down into a thick tapering tail, two small crest nubs at the top, no face, and heavy toed feet. Palette on every facing: blue-grey skin with purple and teal mottling. South and north look far taller and bulkier than east.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale: a squat, heavily plated quadruped in mottled dark-brown and grey-brown with lighter tan banding and speckling. South is a head-on front: a broad hooded head with four small glowing yellow-orange eyes, over a big rounded shovel-like lower jaw edged with jagged teeth, set between thick plated forelegs. East is a side profile walking right: a long low plated body, a protruding upturned shovel jaw with serrated teeth, four yellow eyes in a diagonal row on the side of the head, and a small plate fan at the rear. North is the rear: a domed plated back, a segmented tail knob hanging between the hind legs, and no eyes or face. Clean transparency on all three facings.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution: a plated, armadillo-like segmented shell over the shoulders with tan banding, a central head shield, two pairs of glowing yellow eyes, and a large oval shovel jaw with a row of teeth along the top edge. Squat stance, thick segmented legs with claw toes. No ground shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right: a low, wide plated body with pitted, stony-textured plates in mottled grey-brown. The head is low with a long scoop-shaped lower jaw that juts forward and up, its edge toothed. Four glowing yellow eyes run in a line above the jaw. Four stout legs and a short plated tail fan at the left. No backdrop.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a domed carapace of overlapping plates, with a segmented ridge running down the centre into a hanging tail knob, and hind legs spread at either side. The colouring is mottled brown with some grey-blue cast. No eyes, no face.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom (128 px/cell) the creature is about 2.5 cells long and roughly twice the human's bulk, though lower than the human. It is a dark brown shape on the tan ground. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is still a distinct dark plated shape, larger than the human and much larger than the rat, and the jaw is still legible.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult ossumatha: the same anatomy, pose and silhouette on each facing, but pitch black with blue rim highlights and the same four yellow eyes and shovel jaw.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head on, face toward the camera: four eyes and the shovel jaw facing the viewer.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the domed plated back and a tail knob between the hind legs. No eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are angled game-camera views showing the legs and the body's height. None is an overhead view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured height spread is 13%, within 15%. The south, east and north bodies match the siblings' proportions.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The jaw, the four eyes, the plating, the legs and the tail knob all turn with the body: the jaw is a front oval on south and a jutting scoop on east, and the tail fan shows on east while the knob shows on north. SIGNATURE.seen: The squat plated slab, the shovel-shaped lower jaw and the four glowing yellow eyes are all clearly legible on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The bulk and stance are vaguely rhino-like, but the segmented arthropod-like plating, the jutting toothed shovel jaw and the four glowing eyes keep any stranger from naming it a rhino at first glance.

STYLE.seen: Painterly shading with textured plates. It is not cute, there is no heavy black keyline, and it is not a photo or a 3D render.

OURS.seen: It matches the owner-kept adult's anatomy exactly, recoloured as a commissioned variant. It is not vanilla or other-mod art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean checkerboard transparency around every facing, with no shadow or ground patch.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the siblings panel, painted in a distinct mottled brown and tan colouring instead of black with blue rim light.

SCALE.seen: Beside the human it is about 2.5 cells long, squat and massive, which fits 'a squat slab of... plated muscle' and drawSize 2.5.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a dark plated bulk with a jutting jaw against the tan ground. Contrast is somewhat lower than the black adult's but still clear.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of a stocky four-legged grazer calf on a checkerboard, all at one scale. South and north fill about 400–420 px of height. The east profile stands only about 285 px tall, although its body is long, so the east animal looks clearly smaller than the other two. The hide is a warm taupe-grey with dark smeared streaks. There are two small horn nubs on the crown, rounded hippo-like ears, and a broad snout with a downward fringe of pale, stiff bristles over the mouth.
observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera. Two small dark eyes, two horn nubs on the forehead, rounded ears out to the sides. The broad muzzle ends in a dense curtain of pale cream bristles hanging below the nostrils. The legs are thick and pillar-like with toed feet. Dark grease-like streaks run down the shoulders and legs. The cut-out is clean, with no ground under the feet.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The body is barrel-shaped and the back slopes; a short tufted tail is at the left. The head is lifted and level, with a tapir/rhino-like snout tipped by a bristle fringe. Small horn nub, rounded ear, short legs. Dark diagonal streaks cross the flank and the back. The figure sits low in its canvas and reads smaller than the other facings.
observed.north.png: Rear view: haunches, a hanging tufted tail with a pale tip, back with dark streaks, and the ears and horn nubs seen from behind at the top. No face and no eyes. Hind feet planted. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate stands beside the vanilla human, a little shorter than the human's body and smaller than one cell. In normal play at 32 px/cell it is a small grey four-legged shape, readable against the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult: cooler ash-grey hide with heavy black vertical streaks, a row of dorsal ridge plates along the spine, the head held low in a grazing posture, a black comb-like bristle fringe at the muzzle, a thin dark edge, and no horn nubs.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows haunches and a hanging tail. No face or eyes; only ear backs and horn nubs show at the top.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are at the game-camera angle. None is a top-down view.

The side profile stands fully upright on straight columnar legs, its top of shoulder slab at the same height as the shoulder slab seen in the front and rear views. The side profile is the body length of the young, not a shrunken or crouched figure.

The young wears the adult's hide: cool ash grey, like settled volcanic ash, with black grease-streak shadows running down the shoulders and flanks. The crown is smooth and rounded with no horns and no paired nubs. The muzzle fringe is a dark, near-black comb of filter bristles along both nostrils. A low, soft, budding ridge runs along the spine from shoulder slab to rump, where the adult carries its plates.

The head is a long, low, slab-browed grazing skull carried close to the ground. The muzzle is a flat, wide scoop. The nostrils are fringed with the black filter comb. The ears are small and flat, lying back along the skull. The body is built around a squared, flat-topped slab of shoulder that stands higher than the rump and drops steeply to a low, soft hindquarter. The young's proportions are a larger head, a softer body and slightly shorter legs than the adult.
The side profile keeps the standing shoulder height and body proportions of the front and rear views, with legs straight under the body and the head carried low, the muzzle near knee height.

Give the young small developing versions of the adult's central ridge system: a low unpaired central crest along the midline of the crown, continuing as a row of soft, rounded ridge swellings down the spine. Keep the dark filter combs at full black. Keep the larger head and softer proportions.

Reference: none. The body is built from the description and its departures: slab shoulders, ash-grey hide, black grease-streak shadows, filter-bristle comb at the nostrils, and an integrated ridge along the spine. The silhouette is led by the slab shoulder block and the ridge line, with the combed muzzle as its second signature. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

Body plan: a massive squared slab of shoulder, flat on top and higher than the rump, falling steeply to a low, soft hindquarter. The head is long, low and slab-browed, carried close to the ground. Hide: the exact cool grey of settled volcanic ash, dusty and matte, with darker black grease-streak shadows running down the shoulders and flanks in long smeared bands, streaks that rain never washed away. observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a massive, high-backed grazer seen head-on. Its hide is mossy olive-green and brown, with pale crust patches on the back, leaves lying along the shoulders, a short trunk hanging down, and mud-caked columnar legs. East: a side profile walking right. The hide is olive with copper-orange striping and a pale crust along the spine, with leaves on the back, a tufted tail, a short trunk curled down at the tip, and mud to the knees. North: the rear, showing the haunches and a tufted tail, with no face. The hide here is teal-grey and copper-orange, with a heavy pale crust on the back and a few large leaves. It has no green moss, so the north view is coloured very differently from the south and east views. South stands taller than the other two facings because the hump rises above the head in a head-on view.
observed.south.png: Front view with the face toward the camera: small ears, eyes, and a short wrinkled trunk-lip hanging to chest height. The body is broad with a high domed back, and the hide is moss-green over brown with pale mineral patches. Torn serrated leaves lie along the left shoulder. The four legs are thick, mud-crusted to the knee, with rounded toenails. Clean alpha, painterly and realistic.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing screen right. A high hump rises over the shoulders and the back slopes down to the rump. The tail is thin with a dark tuft. The head is low, the eye half-closed, and the short trunk curls under at the tip. The hide is olive-green with copper-orange stripes along the flank, and a pale crust runs along the spine. A trail of leaves lies along the back and the hip. The legs are mud-caked to the knee. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: broad haunches, a tail tuft in the middle, and four mud-caked legs with toenails. No face or eyes. The hide is blue-teal-grey mottled with copper-orange, a heavy cream mineral crust covers the top of the back, and four or five large leaves lie on it. The colouring is close to the adult sibling's teal and copper, and shows none of the moss-green that the south and east facings of this candidate show.
observed.scale.png: At maximum zoom the candidate stands about 2.8 cells tall and about 4.5 cells long beside a one-cell vanilla human: house-sized. At normal play (32 px per cell) it reads as a large brown-green quadruped with a lighter back. Its contrast against the brown soil is moderate.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult facings. They have the same anatomy, pose and proportions as the candidate: a high-shouldered hump, a short trunk-lip, mud legs and a tufted tail. The hide is teal and copper with a pale crust and leaves. The siblings carry a thin dark outline, which the candidate lacks; the Style law wants no outline. South is also taller than east and north in the sibling set.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. The creature is a wiry, long-legged flier with two pairs of spread, bat-like membranes, a spiky crest and a large bulbous throat sac. South: a front view with an open screaming beak and a teal-green sac. The wings are dark teal with rust-orange blotches and golden-yellow edges, and the body and legs are brown. East: a side profile facing right, beak open, with an orange-to-red sac. Its wings run in a gradient from teal-green at the leading edge to crimson at the trailing edge, edged gold, and the body is olive-brown. North: a rear view showing the back of the crest and the two sac lobes bulging on either side of the neck, with no face. Its wings are orange-brown with cream-yellow radial stripes and lime-green edges, and the body, spine and legs are distinctly green.
observed.south.png: A front view at full resolution. The face is toward the camera, the beak gapes open showing a pink mouth, the eyes sit on either side and a spiky orange crest rises above. A big egg-shaped sac hangs on the throat and chest, teal-green with a fine scale texture. Four membranes are spread: the upper pair is large, the lower pair smaller. The membranes are dark teal mottled with rust-red patches and have saffron-yellow margins. The legs are brown and taloned. The cut-out is clean.
observed.east.png: A right-facing side profile. The open beak and the eye are visible, and the crest sweeps back. A large red-to-yellow-orange sac sits under the jaw. Two wings are visible, one above and behind the other, each a teal-to-crimson gradient with golden edges. The body is slender and olive-brown, the legs are long and taloned, and the cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: A rear view. The back of the head and the crest are visible with no eyes or face, and the two sac lobes show either side of the neck. The back and tail point down. The body and legs are green. All four membranes are spread, orange-rust with cream-yellow banding along the struts and lime-green edges, a pattern unlike both the south and the east facings. The cut-out is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate's east facing stands beside a vanilla human and fills about one cell: smaller than the human and roughly in proportion to drawSize 0.9. At 32 px per cell it reads as a small colourful winged shape beside the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult yammeth: hot magenta membranes with acid-yellow edges and speckles, a plum body, a pink throat sac and a thin dark contour line. The south, east and north poses and silhouettes are near-identical to the candidate's.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head and crest, the spine and the sac lobes from behind. No eyes or face are visible.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera: front, profile and rear. None is a rotated top-down view.

request.prompt: A single yammeth, a light, wiry canopy flier, drawn as a top-down-leaning RimWorld creature sprite in the painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, on a transparent background. Body plan: a slim brown body with long thin brown legs and a small head. Two pairs of broad flight membranes, four in all, spread from the shoulders and hips, a forward pair and a rear pair. Colouring, identical on every facing: all four membranes are deep teal with rust-orange mottling spread across them and a gold band along each edge. Body, head and legs are warm brown. The throat sac under the chin is pale teal-green and puffed out. Eyes are small and dark. These colours and this mottling pattern are the same on the front view (eyes toward the viewer, throat sac in view), the side view (profile, both membrane pairs visible) and the rear view (seen from behind, back and membrane tops in view, face hidden). Flat, simplified shading in broad soft brush shapes with light texture on the membranes and body, matching the kept adult yammeth so the two read as one artist. Transparent background.

observed.facings.png: Three views at one scale on a checkerboard: south, east, north. Each shows a floating headless organism: a cluster of translucent peach-orange swollen sacs, each topped with a puckered, frilled crown. Thin ragged orange membrane fins spread sideways from the cluster's base. Beneath sits a knobbly reddish-brown lumpy mass, and a dense curtain of long, thin, wavy dark-brown tendrils hangs from it. All three views are about the same height. South and north are near-symmetric arrangements. East is an asymmetric cluster with its fins sweeping mostly to the right.
observed.south.png: Symmetric front view. One large central sac with a frilled crown at the top, flanked by two mid-size sacs behind it and two smaller sacs in front, plus one small sac at the bottom centre. The sacs are translucent with glowing orange interiors, faint veins and fine dark speckles. Wavy orange fins project left and right. A knobbly dark red-brown mass lies under the sacs, and many thin dark-brown tendrils hang down roughly a third of the image height. No eyes, no face, no outline, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Side view. The sacs are bunched asymmetrically, with the big one upper left and a second large one to the right. Small sacs are in front, all with frilled crowns. Membrane fins sweep backward to the right and a smaller fin shows on the left. The knobbly mass and the dark tendrils hang below, the tendrils trailing slightly. Soft lighting, no outline, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view, symmetric. A central large sac with a frilled crown, two flanking sacs and two smaller lower sacs, with no small bottom-centre sac (so the sac arrangement differs from south). Fins spread left and right, the knobbly mass shows more of its lumps, and the tendril curtain is dense. No face or eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 1.9 cells wide and about 1.7 cells tall, clearly bigger than the vanilla human. At 32 px/cell it reads as an orange cloud-like blob over a dark fringe, distinct from the tan ground and larger than the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The adult beldon (owner-kept): deeper saturated orange sacs with heavy dark speckles, spiky jagged crests on top, larger jagged fins, a knobbly maroon mass and grey-brown tendrils. The adult is drawn in an illustrated ink-and-watercolour style with thin dark contour lines and a pale rim around each sac. The candidate is smoother, more translucent and softer-lit, with no contour lines.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the cluster with a different sac arrangement; no face or eyes exist anywhere on the creature.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All facings are angled side-on views with the tendrils hanging below; none is a plan view from above.

ALIEN.seen: Canon subject. It reads as a cluster of crowned sacs with fins and a root-like tendril curtain, not a jellyfish bell or a single balloon.

CANON.seen: Lumpy cluster of swollen sacs with puckered frilled crowns, ragged sideways fins, a knobbly mass with a tendril curtain; orange-peach sacs with pale highlights and fine dark speckles; orange fins; reddish-brown underside darker than the sacs; tendrils the darkest element; no purple; no legs, eyes or face; translucent moist membrane, no outlines.

STYLE.seen: Soft painterly realism with translucent membranes and veins; not cute or cel-shaded. Slightly smooth and render-like, but within painterly.

OURS.seen: A new picture, clearly different from the adult sibling and with no donor look.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard; no ground, halo or shadow.

reply.image_seen: The composite and three individual facings show an orange, headless gas-sac cluster with lateral membranes, a reddish knobbly underside and hanging dark tendrils; the scale panel shows it beside a human, and the sibling panel shows more sharply textured adults.

concerns.evidence: The young and adult share speckled orange-peach sacs, puckered crowns, veined orange fins, reddish underside nodules and dark tendril curtains. The young's smaller rounded crowns and softer sac surfaces fit the required juvenile treatment. The adults have stronger pale rims and sharper detailing, but the young retains their organic rendering and recognizable species structure. Its absence of drawn contour lines follows the explicit style law.

The large south sac contains irregular dark freckles, branching internal veins and mottled amber shading beneath an uneven highlight. East shows varied translucency between overlapping sacs, while the fins have fine veins and irregular folds. The underside and tendrils have textured, varied shading. These visible details support the required moist membrane appearance rather than uniformly smooth plastic or a clear 3D-render treatment.

observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera. The head is very broad and blunt, toad- or turtle-like, under a heavy brow, with amber eyes. The mouth is a wide flat slit with reddish lips. There is a short pale central spike plus smaller spikes on the crown. The throat and chest are pale cream-green with folded skin. The four thick short legs have splayed feet and long pale-tan claws. The back and limbs are olive-moss and covered in pebbly scales. The art is painterly and realistic, with no outlines and clean alpha.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The body is low and long, the legs short and thick with splayed clawed feet, and the tail long and tapering. The neck is thick and moderately long, with pale folded skin under the throat. A row of short pale spikes runs from behind the head over the neck. The head is blunt with a reddish-lipped flat mouth. The belly is cream-green, the back olive, the scales pebbly. Clean alpha. The figure fills less of the canvas than south or north.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Back, haunches and the thick tail come toward the camera. The back of the head shows a row of pale spikes down the midline. No face or eyes are visible. The hind feet and claws are splayed to the sides. Pebbly olive hide with paler inner thighs. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the young animal is about 2.5 cells long and clearly larger than the vanilla human. At 32 px/cell it reads as a distinct green lizard shape, larger than the human and the rat, and stands out against the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The kept adult bolotaur. It has a more prominent multi-spike crest, an open toothy mouth, a longer neck, longer legs and darker edge definition. Same olive and cream palette and the same pale claws.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one scale. South: a grey reptavian creature facing the camera, head raised on a moderately long neck, pale tan beak pointing down with two gold hooked prongs at the tip, red-orange eyes, two small horn-like nubs on top of the skull. Long clawed forelimbs plant on the ground, and dark wine-red membranes drape from them like a cape on both sides. Shorter clawed hind feet sit between the forelimbs, and a pointed tail tip hangs behind. East: a true side profile looking right. The body is low and crouched on four clawed limbs, the neck curves up, and the long tan beak ends in a forked gold hook. A short crest of spikes sits at the back of the skull. The folded maroon wing membrane drapes along the flank and forelimb, and a tapering grey tail extends left. North: the rear view. The back of the head shows two nubs and no eyes, the neck rises from the shoulders, the back carries olive mottling, the maroon membranes drape on either side, and a long pointed tail runs straight down toward the viewer between the clawed hind feet. In the panel, south looks somewhat larger than east (feet, claws and head are bigger) and the north is narrower across the wings.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south. Front view with the face toward the camera: the head is somewhat foreshortened, the beak is pale bone with two clearly visible gold prongs, and the eyes are red. The neck has fine scaled texture with a paler throat. The forelimbs are the wing arms, with large curved claws on the ground. The wine-red membranes are folded and spread outward to each side. Painterly with no outline, clean alpha, and no ground shadow.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east. Clean side profile. The skin is finely scaled and wrinkled, slate grey with a faint olive tint on the back. The red-orange eye is visible. The beak is long, toothless and tan, with a two-pronged gold hooked tip. Three or four small crest spikes stand on the occiput. The folded wing membrane is a dark maroon triangle over the forelimb. Climbing claws are on all four feet. The tail is medium length and tapers to a point. No backdrop.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north. Rear view showing the back of the head and two small nubs, with no face or eyes. The neck, back and shoulders carry olive-green mottling, and the maroon membranes drape down both sides. The tail points straight down and toward the viewer. Clawed hind feet show at the bottom. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands beside the vanilla human, roughly two cells long, and its head is at about the human's height. The sail is olive-brown with a translucent membrane and darker ribs, and it is the only crest on the animal. Three views of the same animal share one scale and one body height: the front view (south, eyes and snout toward the viewer, with the sail rising tall behind the head), the side profile (east, head to the right, with the sail rising upright above the back, as high above the back as the body is deep), and the rear view (north, seen from behind, with the back, tail and haunches in view, eyes hidden, and the sail rising above the back at the same height). edits.change: The head carries a pair of branching, tined antlers rising from the top of the skull. Each antler has a main beam with 3 to 4 pointed tines splitting off it, spreading upward and outward like a stag's rack. The antler surface is pale bone-brown, clearly lighter than the dark fur, so the branching reads at small size.

Antlers appear on every facing. South view: both antlers rise symmetrically above the forehead and fan out to either side. East view: the near antler's branching tines show in profile above the head, with the far antler partly behind it. North view: the antlers rise above the rear of the skull with tines spreading left and right, and the face stays hidden.

The back line runs level and flat from the shoulders to the rump, and the shoulders are the same height as the hips. The body is a low, long, barrel-shaped trunk on short, sturdy legs. The chest is broad but not raised.

The head hangs low and wedge-shaped, with a broad flat muzzle and small eyes set far apart. A shaggy fringe of coarse fur hangs from the jaw and throat. The feet are broad, rounded and padded, and the fur is short and coarse on the forequarters, with longer shaggy fur only on the head, throat and flanks.

Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. The antler rack is the first thing a stranger sees, and it makes the creature read as an off-world antlered grazer, not a recoloured bison.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. A lean, tall, four-legged creature with long thin legs ending in pale claws, a long neck and a long narrow blunt-muzzled head. It has two dark brown ridged horns, three dark dorsal spines along the back, and a thin whip tail. The base colour is a pale grey-green or sage. The neck, shoulders and back carry an ochre/yellow-orange pattern. All three facings are about the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view. The face looks toward the camera with two eyes and the blunt muzzle centred. The two horns rise from the top of the skull and curl outward and down in ram-like spirals. The chest is narrow, the forelegs are thin, the claws are pale, and the tail flicks out to the left. Dorsal spines show behind the neck. Mottled ochre covers the neck and shoulders over a sage base. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. A long neck rises steeply and the head sits well above the back. Two long ridged dark horns sweep backward over the neck. Three backward-hooked dorsal spines sit along the back. The waist is tucked, the legs are long and thin with pale claws, and the whip tail is thin. A yellow-ochre reticulated network with darker olive patches covers the top of the neck, the shoulders and the back, and fades out on the flanks. The belly and legs are plain pale sage-grey. Smooth hide, no fur. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: haunches, a tail hanging down the middle, and the back of the neck. Horn curls show at the top. The dorsal spines run down the spine. No face and no eyes. The back and rump carry large ochre-brown blotches over a sage base, bolder and larger than the reticulated net on east. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands about 1.5 to 2 cells long and taller than the human pawn. At 32 px per cell the creature reads as a pale sage, long-necked quadruped with a dark horn accent, distinct from the brown ground, and larger than the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: Reference adult iriaz: the same anatomy, pose, horns, dorsal spines and silhouette, in a darker teal-green base with small rosette-like yellow-orange spots. The candidate matches its build and size, painted in a paler sage base with a bolder ochre reticulated or blotched pattern.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera, with both eyes and the muzzle centred.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the haunches, the tail and the back of the neck. No face or eyes are visible.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn at the game's angled view. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured height spread is 2%, and the facings look matched on the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The horns, the three dorsal spines, the tail, the claws and the palette appear on every facing and turn with the body. The ochre pattern is a finer net on east and bigger blotches on north, which is a minor difference.

SIGNATURE.seen: The long neck, two backward-sweeping horns and the yellow-orange markings over the shoulders and back are clearly legible, most of all on east.

ALIEN.seen: The nearest Earth animal is a gazelle or ibex. The clawed feet, dorsal spines, green hide and odd blunt head stop a stranger naming it as a gazelle. The reticulated pattern hints at a giraffe, but the build does not.

DEPARTURES.seen: Greenish body: present, a sage/grey-green base. Two horns sweeping backward: present, clear on east and curling back on south and north. Yellow-orange spots over the shoulders and back: present, an ochre network or blotches on the neck, shoulders and back.

CANON.seen: Body plan: tall, lean, long thin legs, steep long neck, tucked waist and thin whip tail, with only a small tuft. Horns: two ridged dark horns sweeping back. Colour layout: muted green base with the markings on the neck, shoulders and back, fading toward the belly and legs. Head: long narrow blunt muzzle. Feet: pale claws, no hooves. Hide: smooth, no fur. Rendering: realistic, with no outlines. Negative: not a horse, deer or goat, and not one horn.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with finely textured hide, shaded keratin horns and no keylines. Not cute or cel-shaded.

OURS.seen: Own art that matches the owner-kept iriaz sibling's design. Not a vanilla or donor animal.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. Each facing shows a slender, long-legged, dark-brown, short-coated four-legged hoofed animal with a horse- or foal-like head and neck. There are no horns. A pale cream, segmented, ridged bone plate covers the forehead and the top of the head from between the ears down the nose bridge. South is a front view: the face and plate point at the camera, and the four legs are visible. East is a true side profile walking right, with a long bushy tail, a bristly mane and the bone plate capping the head like a helmet. North is the rear: rump, a long tail hanging down the middle, the back of the neck and the ears, and the ridges of the plate peeking over the poll. North shows no face and no eyes. All three facings are the same size.
observed.south.png: A front view of the dark-brown quadruped. Two upright ears flank a pale ridged bone plate that runs from the forehead down the face to above the dark muzzle. Two dark eyes sit at the sides of the plate. The chest is narrow and the legs are long and thin, with dark hooves. The painterly fur texture has no outline. No ground and no shadow are baked in.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right, mid-stride. The neck is arched and horse-like with a short bristly mane. The pale segmented bone plate wraps the top of the skull from the forehead to behind the ears. The nose is dark. The tail is long and bushy. The legs are slim with small dark hooves. The animal reads as a foal or a light pony. The edges are clean and alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The rear view: haunches, a long brushy tail hanging down the centre and the back of the neck with its mane. Two ears and the top ridges of the bone plate show above the neck. There is no face and there are no eyes. The hind legs and hooves are clean. No ground is baked in.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal stands about as tall as the vanilla human and about two cells long, which is pony-sized. At 32 px per cell it reads as a dark-brown four-legged silhouette that stands well apart from the tan ground, with the pale head plate still visible as a light spot.
observed.siblings.png: The reference sibling (the male Kybuck) is a different design: a golden-tan, white-bellied, antelope- or goat-like animal standing upright on its hind legs. edits.change: The coat is deep dark brown across the whole body, with a slightly lighter brown on the belly and inner legs. The body is a slender, long-legged, four-legged antelope-like ungulate with a narrow chest, a light trunk, a long neck and cloven hooves. The creature always stands on all four legs, the same four-legged plan as the canon description.

The female uses the species' one shared design: dark-brown coat, slender four-legged ungulate build and the same facial bone plate, painted in the same painterly vanilla RimWorld style as her male counterpart. The only sex difference is the head crown: her crown between the ears is smooth and bare, where the male carries spiral horns.

The head is narrow and wedge-shaped, like an antelope's: a short, fine muzzle, a small dark nose, large upright leaf-shaped ears set high on the skull and large dark eyes set on the sides of the head. One large pale bone-coloured plate covers the face from the brow ridge down to the nose bridge. It has a ridged, slightly rough surface and is clearly the most prominent feature of the face, visible in the front view and in the side view as a pale shield over the dark-brown head.
Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette. The pale bone plate and the dark-brown body give the clearest contrast against the transparent ground.

invariants: dark-brown coat (kept from the first render, which matched the canon description)
four-legged quadruped stance
hornless female crown
large bone plate across the face as the one departure from an Earth ungulate
transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic
drawSize 1.8 x 1.8 proportions
request.prompt: A female kybuck, a swift sociable ungulate from Kashyyyk, drawn as a single creature sprite for RimWorld on a transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette. Body: slender, long-legged, four-legged antelope-like ungulate standing on all four legs, with a narrow chest, a light trunk, a long neck, slim legs ending in cloven hooves and a short tail. The coat is deep dark brown over the whole body, slightly lighter brown on the belly and inner legs, with soft fur texture and gentle light and shade that give the body volume. Head: narrow and wedge-shaped like an antelope's, with a short fine muzzle, a small dark nose, large upright leaf-shaped ears set high on the skull and large dark eyes on the sides of the head. A large pale bone-coloured plate with a ridged, slightly rough surface covers the face from the brow ridge to the nose bridge. It is the most striking feature of the face and shows as a pale shield over the dark-brown head. The crown of the head between the ears is smooth and bare, because the female has no horns. The same design (dark-brown coat, slender four-legged build, narrow head, upright ears and facial bone plate) is used in every facing. Front view: the face and the bone plate look toward the viewer, with both ears and both eyes visible. Side view: the full profile shows the wedge-shaped head, the bone plate, the long neck and the four legs in a walking stance. Rear view, seen from behind: the haunches, the short tail and the backs of the ears, with the face hidden.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a flat, broad, lobed disc-like body with a leaf-shaped head at front centre showing two amber eyes and a small dark-purple hooked beak, a tall crown of pink-to-magenta tendrils rising from the nape, and six pale grey-green translucent paddle legs with curved violet claw tips splayed below. East: a long side profile with the head at right (eye and purple beak), tendrils swept back over the nape, a fish-like fluked tail at left, and six paddle legs hanging below in three pairs. North: the rear disc, no face, a tendril crown, six paddle legs, and the fluked tail hanging down at centre. The colouring is cool sage/grey-green with dark green vein streaks and large magenta-purple rosette spots, on all three facings.
observed.south.png: Front view, full resolution. The face is toward the camera: two amber eyes and a dark-purple beak sit on a leaf-shaped head plate in front of a wider lobed disc. Magenta tendril crown. Six clawed paddle legs, pale grey-green with purple spots and violet claws. Painterly, finely veined, no outline, clean alpha, no ground.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. A low elongated body with a dark-streaked sage back and magenta rosettes, the head at right with an amber eye and a hooked purple beak, crimson tendrils streaming back, and a forked fluke tail at left. Six legs are visible as three overlapping pairs of paddle limbs with violet claws. The east figure is shorter than the other facings because the tendrils sweep back rather than up. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: the back of the disc with a central dark-green vein pattern, the pink tendril crown seen from behind, and no eyes or beak. The fluked tail hangs down at centre between six clawed paddle legs. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human at max zoom, the creature is about 2 cells long, longer than the human is wide and about his height including the tendrils. At 32 px/cell the pink tendril tuft and the grey-green body read against the brown ground; the legs blur into a fringe.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult ollopom: the same anatomy, pose and silhouette on all three facings (lobed disc, beaked leaf head, pink tendril crown, six paddle legs, fluked tail), coloured olive-yellow-green with small purple speckles. The sibling's east is also shorter than its south and north.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on: two amber eyes and a purple beak centred on the leaf-shaped head.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the disc and the tail hanging down; no eyes or beak.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera: legs hang below the disc, and the east is a profile. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured 18% height spread comes from the east pose: the tendrils sweep back instead of standing up. Body width and leg length match across the facings, and the owner-kept sibling shows the same east-shorter pattern.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Disc, tendril crown, six paddle legs, fluke tail and the rosette/streak palette are present on every facing. The tail trails behind in east and hangs at centre in north, so the tail turns with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The pink head tendrils are the brightest element and dominate the silhouette on every facing; the lily-pad disc body is clear.

ALIEN.seen: A six-legged lily-pad disc with a beaked leaf head, a tendril crown and a fish fluke reads as no Earth animal. The def text names a rodent, but nothing in the art reads as a rodent.

DEPARTURES.seen: six legs: present (three pairs, clear in south/north, overlapped in east); green fur: present (sage grey-green, painted as a smooth leafy surface rather than fur, as on the sibling); gnawing teeth on the underside: not visible, because no game facing shows the underside, and the owner-kept adult also shows none; three pairs of paddle-like claws: present (leaf-paddle legs with violet hooked claws); flukes as rudders: present (forked fluke tail in east and north).

CANON.seen: BODY PLAN: flat oval disc body, large leaf-shaped head, six paddle clawed legs, long fluked tail – yes. COLOUR LAYOUT: green with round magenta/purple spots, including on the tail; pink tendrils brightest; pale translucent grey-green legs with violet claw tips – yes. The base hue is shifted cool grey-green with dark streaks, which is the variant's job. Tendril cluster from the nape – yes. Small dark-purple beak, amber eyes – yes. NEGATIVE: not a brown rodent and not a submerged swimmer – yes.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, finely veined surfaces, soft shading, no keyline. The eyes are small and natural, not glossy or cute.

OURS.seen: Original painted art matching the owner-kept adult's design; not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on all facings: no water, pad, ground or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The anatomy, pose, size and silhouette match the adult in siblings.png almost one-for-one. The colouring is clearly distinct: cool sage with dark vein streaks and large magenta rosettes, against the adult's olive-yellow with fine speckles. It reads as the same species, a different colour morph.

SCALE.seen: About 2 cells long beside the human, the same size class as the adult at drawSize 1.75. That is a little large for 'squat, short', but it matches the owner-kept sibling.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the magenta tuft and the pale green body read as separate bold shapes against the ground. The legs merge into a fringe, which is acceptable.

findings.seen: The creature spans about 2 cells, roughly as tall as the human including the tendrils, for an animal described as 'short' and 'squat'.
findings.quote: Scale beside the human against the description's size words … Both are polish.
findings.fix: Keep the sprite matched to the owner-kept adult's canvas size; a smaller drawSize for the species is a def-side tweak if the owner wants it.

proposals: The 'gnawing teeth on the underside' departure cannot be shown by any game facing (the camera never sees the underside); consider marking that departure as an engine limit on the card so reviewers do not have to judge it.

polish.quote: Scale beside the human against the description's size words … Both are polish.
polish.fix: Keep the sprite matched to the owner-kept adult's canvas size; a smaller drawSize for the species is a def-side tweak if the owner wants it.

reply.subject: RSW_Pufferpig__young

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a squat, round, barrel-bodied creature facing the camera. Its warm amber-brown hide carries a darker brown polygon/honeycomb blotch pattern. Two sleepy heavy-lidded teal eyes sit in raised fleshy brow mounds. A wrinkled trunk hangs from the middle of the face to a small flared tip. Two short pale horns grow from the crown, with pale conical spikes around the top edge. Four stubby pillar legs end in dark toes. East: a right-facing profile of the same animal, with a pale spike row along the back, a trunk hanging down at the front, a teal eye and short legs. The east body is drawn visibly smaller (shorter and less tall) than south and north. North: the rear, showing a rounded back with the blotch pattern, a central row of pale spikes running down into a short spiky tail ridge, and horn tips visible over the back. There is no face and no eyes. Haunches and four legs show from behind.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south: a front view, face to the camera. The trunk is wrinkled and hangs to a flared tip. The eyes are teal and heavy-lidded. Two small horns and a spike fringe sit on top. The hide is thick and wrinkled. Lighting is soft and natural, with no outline. The cut-out is clean on transparency.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east: a true side profile facing right. The trunk curls down at the front, there is a spike row along the spine, the blotch pattern covers the back and head, and the hide on the legs is wrinkled. The figure sits lower in the canvas and is smaller than the south figure. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: the rear view, with a spine spike row running into a tail ridge, the back pattern, and wrinkled haunches. There are no eyes and no face. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human at max zoom, the creature is about knee-to-hip high and roughly a cell long, a small animal. At 32 px/cell it reads as a small orange-brown oval with pale spike flecks, set apart from the tan ground by its warmer, darker tone.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult Pufferpig: the same body plan (barrel body, hanging trunk, heavy-lidded eyes on brow mounds, honeycomb pattern, stubby legs, dark toes). The adult palette is olive/sage-to-sand with a paler honeycomb, and its horns and spikes are dark slate-black and larger. The adult also has an inflated, rounder body.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The face, trunk and both eyes look straight at the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, the spine spikes, the tail ridge and the haunches, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are at the game's angled camera. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: East is visibly smaller than south and north on the shared-scale panel: its body is roughly two-thirds their height and does not reach the same vertical extent. The measured spread is 53%. The difference is not a pose: a standing profile of a barrel body should be about as tall as its front view.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same palette, honeycomb pattern, pale horns, spine spikes and trunk appear on every facing. The horns and spike row turn correctly with the body (front pair on south, profile on east, a central spine row on north).

SIGNATURE.seen: The flexible wrinkled trunk-snout is prominent on south and east. The barrel body reads clearly. Inflation is a behaviour, not a sprite requirement.

ALIEN.seen: The trunk recalls an elephant, but a stranger would not name it an elephant or a pig at first glance. The fat barrel body, honeycomb hide, crown horns, spine spikes and turret eyes make it its own creature.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure 'flexible snout, not a pig's rigid disc snout': present. A hanging, ringed, flexible trunk with a flared tip; there is no disc.

CANON.seen: BODY PLAN: small barrel body, stubby legs, big blunt head, little neck, dark toes, spiky tail ridge on north (present). COLOUR: tan/amber hide with a darker honeycomb, teal eyes (present). TRUNK: hanging, wrinkled, flared tip (present). EYES: heavy-lidded, sleepy, on raised fleshy brow mounds; more turret-like mounds than true stalks, but they read (present). HORNS and SPIKES: a short curved crown pair and a spine row, in pale ivory, which canon allows (present). REALISTIC wrinkled hide, no outline (present). NEGATIVE: not pig-pink, no disc snout, not a smooth blob (satisfied).

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with wrinkled elephant-like hide, natural lighting and no keyline. The sleepy eyes come from canon and are not cute-glossy. The rendering slightly suggests a 3D render, but it matches the owner-kept adult.

OURS.seen: Own commissioned art (artpipe jobs listed). It does not match any vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: A clean cut-out on transparency for all facings. There is no ground patch or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: It reads as a young Pufferpig: small budding horns and spikes, a smaller body than the adult, and the same body plan and features. The warm brown palette and ivory spikes differ from the adult's olive tone and dark spikes, which weakens the same-species read somewhat. The shape, trunk, eyes and pattern still carry the read.

SCALE.seen: Beside the human it is a small, dog-sized animal, which suits a young animal of size 0.5.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a compact warm-brown oval with spike flecks, distinct from the ground.

findings.seen: On the shared-scale panel, the east profile body is about 150 px tall against about 230 px for south and about 205 px for north. The east animal looks clearly smaller than the other two views.
findings.quote: it needs the treatment that makes the different facings the same size.
findings.fix: Scale the east profile so its body height and bulk match the south and north views of the same young animal.

findings.seen: The young is a warm orange-brown with a dark-brown honeycomb and pale ivory horns and spikes. The owner-kept adult is olive/sage-sand with a pale honeycomb and slate-black horns and spikes, so the palettes of the young and adult differ noticeably.

subject: RSW_Ronto__young

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South: a front view of a stocky, olive-grey, four-legged reptile. The face looks at the camera. The head carries a small nose horn, a beak and two large rounded, scalloped, cream-lined ear flaps; small spikes form a crest on top of the head. East: a true side profile looking right. The body is barrel-shaped, the neck medium-long and rising, and the tail short and pointed. The ear flap fans back behind the head. North: the rear. The back is striped and the short tail tip points down. The ear flaps fan out on each side and the small head spikes show at the top. No face or eyes. All three facings look about the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. A triangular head with a downturned beak, two small eyes and a short rhino-like nose horn. Two large frill-like ear flaps have scalloped edges, veining and a pale cream inner face. Small spike buds sit on top of the skull. The neck is thick and deeply creased with a cream throat. The body is olive-grey-brown with darker striping on the flanks and scattered warts. The four legs are columnar and ringed with wrinkles, and the broad feet carry blunt hoof-claws. Clean alpha. No ground and no shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. The neck rises in a gentle curve to a beaked head with a nose horn. The ear flap is a large fan, cream on its inner side, and spreads back from the skull. Dark bands run across the neck and back. The hide is wrinkled, with wart bumps along the spine. The belly is paler. The legs are thick and columnar, with wrinkled joints and hoofed, clawed feet. The tail is short, thick and tapered. Clean cut-out.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back is broad and striped, with wart bumps. A short thick tail points down over a pale underside. Four columnar legs show, the near pair larger. The neck rises to the back of the head. The two ear flaps fan out sideways and their rear surfaces look pale, ribbed and veined. Small spike tips show at the top of the head. No eyes or face are visible. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Max zoom: the young ronto is about 3 cells tall and about 4 cells long, much bigger than the vanilla human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a large grey-brown quadruped with a fanned head, clearly bigger than the human and the rat. Its silhouette stands apart from the tan ground.
observed.siblings.png: The adult ronto, owner-kept, with saddle and harness. It is lankier, with a much longer S-curved neck and a small head. Its ear flaps are bat-wing fans. Its hide matches the candidate: olive-grey with dark neck striping and warts. Its legs are columnar with dark hoof-claws, and its tail is moderate. Its palette and rendering style match the candidate.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, the striping, the short tail and the hind legs. The back of the head and the ears show, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are at the game's angled camera. None is a top-down view.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The ear flaps, nose horn, head spikes, striping, warts and short tail appear on every facing where they can be seen. The ear flaps turn with the body: they spread sideways on south and north and fan backward in the east profile.

SIGNATURE.seen: The broad earflaps are the most visible feature on every facing. The long neck and wrinkled hide are clear.

ALIEN.seen: This is a canon subject. It reads as a ronto-like saurian, not as an elephant or a sauropod: it has a beak, a nose horn, fanned ears and no trunk or tusks.

DEPARTURES.seen: Broad earflaps on the head: present, large and fanned on all facings. Wrinkled hide: present, with deep creases on the neck, legs and body.

CANON.seen: Body plan: a four-legged saurian on columnar legs with hoofed, clawed feet. The neck is shortened for a young animal but rises in a gentle curve, and the tail is short and thick. Nose horn and downturned beak: present. Wing-like skin-flap ears: present. Wrinkles and warts: present. Colour: olive-to-brownish-grey with dark neck and back striping and a cream underside and inner ear. Realistic and outline-free. Not a sauropod and not an elephant.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with a detailed wrinkled hide and soft lighting. No keylines and no cel shading. The face is stern, with small eyes, not cute.

OURS.seen: This is commissioned art (the xart jobs) and it matches the kept adult's style. It is not vanilla art or another mod's art.

ALPHA.seen: The checkerboard shows through around the body on every facing. No ground patch or shadow is baked in.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a bulky grey-brown body, a rising neck and a fanned head, set apart from the tan ground.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. South: a long-legged tan quadruped faces the camera. It has a ringed, wrinkled trunk-like snout, a small pale tusk on each side of the mouth, wide brown ears held out to the sides, and a shaggy orange-gold forelock and mane. The body has brown blotches. The cream hooves are two-toed. A dark tail brush shows between the hind legs. East: a right-facing side profile. The legs are long with knobby knees, and an orange-gold mane runs from the poll along the neck to the mid-back. The head is wrinkled and blunt, with a short curled trunk boss. Two small pale tusks curve down from the jaw and hook forward at the tips. The long ears sweep back. The thin tail ends in a dark brush at about hock height. North: the rear view. It shows the back of the head with the mane, the ears out to the sides, the mottled rump, the tail and its dark brush, and the hind legs. No face or eyes are visible. The three facings are a similar size.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south: a frontal view of the face, with the ringed trunk in the centre, small eyes, two small pale tusks under the trunk, wide dark-lined ears, and a shaggy gold forelock. The chest is mottled. The legs are slender with knobby joints. The cream hooves are split into two toes. The alpha is clean, with no ground.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east: a true right-facing profile with a painterly, realistic hide texture. The coat has large irregular brown blotches on sandy tan. The coarse mane is darker gold. The ears are brown. The hooves are cream and the lightest element. Tusks hang down from the jaw line and curl forward. There are small wrinkle bumps on the brow and snout but no distinct horn nubs. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: the rear. The mane runs down the back of the neck, the ears spread to the sides, the blotchy rump sits above a tail with a dark brush, and the hind legs end in cream two-toed hooves. No face appears. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate is drawn across about 2 cells and stands taller than the vanilla human. In normal play at 32 px per cell it reads as a tan long-legged quadruped with a light head and dark tail, distinct from the brown ground but low in contrast. Its body colour is close to the ground colour.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult. The south view has a large head with big black down-and-out curving horns, a trunk boss and upturned tusks, a fine-speckled pale golden hide and a heavy mane. The east view has very spindly long legs, a lowered head and tusks rising from the lower jaw. The north view shows the rear. The adult's hide is finely speckled and paler gold, where the candidate has bolder, redder-brown patches.
