East: a right-facing profile on long thin legs, a high stance, a long narrow muzzle, large ears, and a ridge of blue-white crystal shards along the neck, shoulders and spine, running into a long tail made of crystal spikes. North: the rear, with the backs of both ears, a crest of shards at the nape, a shard-covered back, the tail hanging straight down the middle, and hind legs. No face appears on north. Facings are similar in height. No outline. Soft painterly shading.

Front view at full resolution. Face toward the camera, eyes pale blue, small dark nose, inner ears pinkish-grey. The head and chest are covered in overlapping pale faceted plates. The legs are smooth grey with few facets. The tail of translucent blue-white crystal points sweeps to the left. Clean alpha, no ground or shadow.

True side profile facing right. Leggy, upright, almost deer-like stance. Spiky translucent crystal shards stand up along the nape, shoulders and back. The tail is a long brush of blue crystal spikes, held out behind. The lower body and legs are smoother grey. Eye blue. Clean alpha.

Rear view: the backs of two large ears, a starburst crest of shards at the back of the head, a back layered with crystal plates, and a blue-tinted crystal tail hanging down between the hind legs. No eyes or face. Clean alpha.

At max zoom, the candidate stands beside the vanilla human, about as long as one cell plus a little, and slightly shorter than the human's head-plus-body. At 32 px per cell it reads as a pale grey-blue fox shape with a spiky tail, clearly apart from the brown ground, larger than the rat.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one scale. South: a squat, domed animal seen face-on. Overlapping terracotta plates cover it, with a cracked-clay texture and pale cream star-shaped seams. Two small blunt horns sit on top. Two small eyes sit under a plated brow, with a blunt, slightly downturned snout. Four thick, wrinkled, columnar legs end in clawed toes. East: the same animal in a true right-facing profile: a long low body under shingled cracked plates, horns on the shoulders, a blunt rounded head with a small eye, and four short legs with claws. It is drawn visibly smaller than the other two: shorter top-to-toe, with smaller feet. North: the rear. A big tail-end plate hangs down over the rump, the two horns show over the top, two hind legs with clawed feet sit below, and there is no face or eyes.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. Domed cracked-clay carapace of plate-like scutes, cream star seams, two budding horns, a plated brow over small dark eyes, and a broad blunt muzzle. Thick legs are splayed under the body with clawed toes. Clean alpha, no ground under it.
observed.east.png: Side profile looking right. Elongated body, shingled terracotta plates with cream star cracks, two small horns behind the head, and a rounded blunt snout with a nostril and a small eye. Four short clawed legs are visible, the body sitting fairly high on them. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A broad domed back of cracked plates, horn tips at the top, a large pointed rear plate over the rump, and two hind feet with clawed toes. No face, no eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about one cell wide and stands well below the human's waist. In normal play at 32 px per cell, it is a small reddish-brown oblong beside the rat. The reddish brown is close in value to the tan ground but distinct in hue.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult. A very low mound of flat, angular clay slabs, like a pile of broken adobe, with thick pale yellow wax running in seams between the slabs. A pointed wedge snout with tiny slit eyes. Only flat flipper-like toe pads show at the base, with no visible legs. No horns. It reads as a rock or clay heap that is alive.

OURS.seen: It is own art. It matches no vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: All three facings are clean cut-outs: no ground patch, shadow or halo.

reply.image_seen: The shared-scale panel and three individual sprites show a reddish plated quadruped from front, right side and rear; the scale panel places it beside a human, and the sibling panel shows a low, wedge-snouted adult with broad wax-filled seams.

concerns.evidence: In south and east, the young has substantial exposed legs, conspicuous claws and a blunt, broad muzzle. The adult reference has barely exposed feet and a pointed wedge snout continuous with its low armored body. The young also introduces paired horn buds without a visible adult counterpart. Although both share reddish plates and pale seams, the combined anatomical changes weaken the required same-species appearance; the young's more elevated stance particularly conflicts with the requested shorter legs.

The adult east silhouette is a low mound of angular, overlapping clay slabs tapering into the snout, with thick pale wax between plates. The candidate east shows a distinct rounded head, raised torso and muscular legs beneath more regularly domed armor; south emphasizes wrinkled flesh and sculpted facial anatomy. Shared colors and painterly rendering provide continuity, but the difference in body construction and surface treatment is substantial.

In the shared-scale panel, east has visibly smaller horn buds, feet and limb thickness than south and north, alongside its lower overall height. Its legs remain extended in a standing pose, so crouching does not explain the measured 44% height spread. The discrepancy extends beyond the expected difference between front and side silhouettes.

request.prompt: A young tammuq, a small burrowing creature of dry cracked-pan flats, painted in the painterly realistic style of vanilla RimWorld on a transparent background. It is a smaller, rounder version of the adult. Its body is a low, wide, ground-hugging mound of flat angular dry-clay slab plates, like broken adobe, in dull tan and ochre. Thick pale yellow wax fills the seams between the slabs, running in wide bands. The slab faces are flat and planar, with low surface detail. The belly rests close to the ground in a crouch. The head is slightly larger for the body than the adult's. It is smooth and hornless, and ends in a short pointed wedge snout with narrow slit eyes. Only stubby flat toe pads show under the rim of the mound, and the legs stay hidden under the slabs. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast between the clay slabs, the pale wax and the ground carry the silhouette. No outlines. Three facings drawn at one shared scale: the south view is the front, with the wedge snout and slit eyes toward the viewer; the east view is a side profile of the mound with the snout pointing to one side; the north view is the rear, seen from behind, showing the back slabs and haunches with the eyes hidden. In every facing the mound has the same body height (about 340 px on a 1.0 draw-size canvas), the same head size and the same toe-pad size, so the east profile matches the south and north views. Lit from the upper left, with a soft shadow under the rim.
